Activates when an enemy is neutralized while in the Ensnaring Chains state. Affects self. Restraint Chain ▲ 1, up to 10.

caveats: ⚑ The skill1 chain-dump has NO activation clause in the kit ("at a specific timing") — the interval trigger sec:10 is an invented cadence. Because the block is gated on a FULL Restraint Chain pool, the cadence only sets the latency between a refill and the dump, not the number of dumps; total dump damage per cycle is cadence-insensitive so long as the interval fires at least once per refill cycle.

The dump block is gated resourceGate{restraintChain,min:10} because flatDamage cannot scale its hit count by a live pool. In this fight the pool is only ever 0 or 10 (both charge lines fill to cap; the +1-on-neutralize line is inert vs a raid boss), so a fixed 10-hit dump is exact here. On any fight where the pool can sit partial, this block UNDER-fires (0 hits) rather than over-firing.

⚑ Ensnaring Chains stack accrual is read as +1 per chain attack (the DoT paragraph directly follows the attack paragraph and says "the same enemy units"), i.e. +10 per dump. The kit does not state the per-attack stack grant explicitly.

Ensnaring Chains is modeled as ONE passive perResource DoT reading the ensnaringStack pool, not as N appended DoT instances — the engine never dedups appended instances and could not honour the 20-stack cap nor the burst's cancel.

⚑ Dragging Chain mirrors the live Ensnaring stack count, but no effect can copy one pool into another, and a perResource DoT would read 0 after the cancel. It is therefore authored as a fixed 500.5% = 10 mirrored stacks × 50.05%, the derived steady-state (10 chains per dump, cancelled every burst, rebuilt at the next FB-end refill). It under-credits the skill2 in-FB stack adds present at cast.

The skill2 40-normal-attack rider counts CUMULATIVE rounds with an inFb gate rather than resetting its counter per Full Burst window, so its fire count is an approximation of "40 normal attacks during Full Burst".

⚑ MG cadence tuple (pulls/s, wind-up ladder, reloadFrames 171) comes from the datamine and is unreliable; every dump/DoT total scales with the resulting shot count only through the skill2 rider, but the normal-attack bucket depends on it directly.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Mihara: Bonding Chain is modeled as a two-pool kit. `restraintChain` (init 10, cap 10) is the ammunition for skill1's chain dump: a pool-full-gated block fires 10 discrete 50.06%-of-final-ATK crit-eligible hits, spends all 10 chains, and adds 10 stacks to `ensnaringStack` (cap 20). The pool refills to cap when Full Burst ends on a rotation this unit actually cast her own burst (ownBurstGate 'cast'). Ensnaring Chains is a single passive sustained-flavour DoT ticking every 1s for the fight, its per-tick magnitude driven live by the ensnaringStack pool at 25.08% per stack; DoT crit is left at the engine default (off). skill2 adds one stack per 40 cumulative normal-attack rounds while in Full Burst on an already-ensnared target, and grants self Sustained Damage ▲59.98% for 10s on entering Burst Stage 3. The burst applies Dragging Chain — a 10s, 1s-interval sustained DoT authored at a fixed 500.5% (⚑ 10 mirrored stacks × 50.05%) — then cancels Ensnaring Chains by zeroing the stack pool, so the Ensnaring DoT goes silent until the next refill-and-dump cycle rebuilds it. Deliberately unmodeled: the incapacitation stack burst and the on-neutralize chain refund (no death or enemy-neutralize events exist in the v1 raid scope).

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #2: the chain-dump damage line carries NO activation clause ("at a specific timing"), so both the trigger kind and its cadence are invented. 10s is the common internal-cooldown magnitude for a kit-silent recurring damage line. Because the block is gated on a FULL chain pool, the cadence changes only the refill→dump latency, not the dump count, so the total is largely cadence-insensitive.
flags.recipe: Frame-read a recording: timestamp the first burst of 10 chain popups relative to t=0 (that is the first-fire phase) and the gap between the FB-end refill and the next popup burst (that is the interval). If the popups instead arrive one-per-tick rather than as a volley, the whole 'dump all chains at once' reading is wrong — re-model as a per-attack cadence.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #4: Dragging Chain mirrors the Ensnaring stack count at cast, a live currency. Derived steady state: the chain pool fills to 10 at battle start and again at every FB-end following her own burst; each dump converts 10 chains into 10 Ensnaring stacks; her burst cancels Ensnaring, so the pool is ~10 at every cast. The skill2 in-FB rider adds a small unmodelled excess (roughly +1 per 40 in-FB rounds), so 10 is a conservative floor, not a fitted value.
flags.recipe: Read the Dragging Chain tick value off a fight: divide one tick's damage by (0.5005 × final ATK) to recover the mirrored stack count directly, and compare the first-burst count (battle-start dump only) against later bursts (refill dump + FB riders). If the counts differ across bursts, replace the constant with a mirrored pool + per-stack dot effects.

flags.estimate: +1 Ensnaring stack per chain attack (+10 per dump)
flags.reasoning: The kit states the Ensnaring paragraph applies to "the same enemy units" as the chain attacks but never states the per-attack stack grant. 1-per-attack is the natural reading and is what makes the 20-stack cap and the burst mirror meaningful; the alternative (a single stack per dump activation) would make the 20 cap nearly unreachable.
flags.recipe: Count Ensnaring tick magnitude growth after a single dump: 10 stacks predicts a 10× jump in the per-second sustained tick vs 1 stack. One popup read of two consecutive Ensnaring ticks straddling a dump discriminates them.

flags.reasoning: The kit says "40 normal attacks DURING Full Burst", implying a counter scoped to (and probably reset per) the FB window. The engine's hitCount is a cumulative round counter; the fbGate suppresses out-of-FB firings but does not reset the tally, so out-of-FB rounds still advance it. This OVER-fires relative to a per-window counter.
flags.recipe: MG rounds are fast enough that 40 in-FB rounds are plausible within one 10s window — count her rounds inside a single FB from footage (or the sim's shot events) and compare the number of Ensnaring stack gains observed per FB against the modeled count.
